analysis.successDefinition: All of the following are observable in the post-horizon code on disk and green under packages/llm-http-proxy's gate stack (npm run lint + npm run typecheck + npm test): (1) packages/llm-http-proxy/package.json declares `undici` in `peerDependencies` and `peerDependenciesMeta.undici.optional: true`; (2) src/interceptor.ts Interceptor.install() unconditionally patches both http.ClientRequest.prototype.write/end/on and the undici global dispatcher captured via getGlobalDispatcher()/setGlobalDispatcher(), invoking the existing emitLogEntry builder for both surfaces so the captured LlmLogEntry shape is byte-identical between transports; (3) Interceptor.restore() reinstalls the original undici dispatcher by reference identity AND is idempotent; (4) install() called twice on the same instance is a no-op (kDispatcherWrapper symbol-tag guard); (5) when the `undici` peer is absent at runtime, install() still patches the http surface and silently skips the undici side; (6) a new test file at packages/llm-http-proxy/src/global-fetch-capture.integration.test.ts proves global fetch is captured via the undici-patch surface by calling globalThis.fetch against a localhost mock HTTP server and asserting entries.length === 1 with the expected LlmLogEntry fields; (7) src/index.ts public surface is unchanged; (8) the in-source comment at lines 225-228 is rewritten to describe dual-surface coverage; (9) the package's dependencies block remains {}; (10) the existing fetch-baseline.integration.test.ts and the 3 raw-HTTPS integration tests still pass without modification.
assumptions: The horizon's primary proof surface is a single new test that uses global fetch against a localhost mock HTTP server; the SDK test files do not exist on disk (horizon-8 is 'planned', not 'completed') and are NOT in scope per the user's Step-0 redirect.

undici is bundled inside Node 18+ as globalThis.fetch's implementation, but is NOT reachable as a user-importable module; require('undici') throws MODULE_NOT_FOUND unless the undici npm package is explicitly installed. The horizon adds it as an optional peer dep.

When undici is declared as an optional peer dep and installed via npm/pnpm install, the lazy-require inside the interceptor returns a non-undefined undici object; install() then performs the dual-patch.

When undici is NOT installed (e.g., a consumer's downstream package manager decides not to install the peer), the lazy-require returns undefined; install() silently skips the undici side and still patches http.ClientRequest.prototype — preserving horizon-7/8 behavior. No thrown error, no behavioral regression.
setGlobalDispatcher(original) is the documented undici round-trip; passing null throws TypeError. The restore() must reinstate by reference identity.
Interceptor.install() gains no new option — the dual-patch is unconditional, per the user's Step-0 answer.
src/index.ts is not touched — no new export, no version bump.

The undici-patch surface receives a plain DispatchOptions object, not a stateful ClientRequest. The horizon builds a synthetic ClientRequest from DispatchOptions (duck-typed via the existing `as unknown as { ... }` view-cast discipline in interceptor.ts:905-921) so the existing emitLogEntry builder can be reused verbatim.
The capture-decision gate (shouldCapture by hostname against this.providers) applies to BOTH surfaces — a fetched URL whose hostname is not in the providers list does not produce an entry.

The fetch-baseline integration test (src/fetch-baseline.integration.test.ts) remains unchanged; it exercises the http.ClientRequest.prototype surface via node:https.request and continues to pass without modification.
The new test uses plain HTTP because global fetch over loopback works fine without TLS setup (fetch-baseline needed HTTPS because it exercises node:https.request).
risks: The undici npm package version pinned in peerDependencies may drift over time; if a future major release of undici changes the Dispatcher interface, the wrapping dispatcher would need to be updated.
setGlobalDispatcher() is process-global; tests that mutate it could leak state between files and produce flaky ordering-dependent failures.

The synthetic ClientRequest built from DispatchOptions must satisfy every field emitLogEntry/deriveUrl/resolveScheme probe via view-casts; if any field is missing or wrong, the LlmLogEntry shape diverges from the http-patch surface.
The kDispatcherWrapper Symbol-tag idempotency guard must match the existing kWriteWrapper/kEndWrapper pattern.

Double-emission risk: if a test fires a httpsRequest AND a globalThis.fetch for the same logical request, both surfaces emit (no de-duplication). Mitigation: the new test uses global fetch ONLY; existing tests use https.request ONLY.
The horizon's test surface does NOT prove SDK-driven fetch traffic (via @ai-sdk/* provider factories) is actually captured — that proof requires the SDK test files from horizon-8 to land first.

If a consumer's downstream package manager doesn't install the undici peer, install() silently degrades and the user gets no diagnostic. The horizon's success criterion #5 says 'silently skips' which contradicts emitting a log.
The horizon's 'graceful degradation' assumption depends on the lazy-require NOT throwing on Node 18+ (it does not).
The misleading-comment update at lines 225-228 must not delete the existing 'https.ClientRequest IS http.ClientRequest' fact.

discoveryFindings.finding: Node 22.14.0 bundles undici 6.21.1 as `globalThis.fetch`'s implementation but it is NOT reachable as a user-importable module: `require('undici')` from any path throws MODULE_NOT_FOUND. Only undici-types@6.21.0 (types-only) is on disk as a transitive of @types/node@22.20.1.
discoveryFindings.implication: The horizon MUST add `undici` as an optional peer dependency so install() can lazy-require it at runtime and gracefully degrade to undici-patch-disabled if absent.

discoveryFindings.finding: The Dispatcher class shape from undici-types@6.21.0: `dispatch(options: Dispatcher.DispatchOptions, handler: Dispatcher.DispatchHandlers): boolean` plus connect/compose/request/pipeline/stream/upgrade/close/destroy + EventEmitter. DispatchOptions fields include origin/path/method/body/headers. DispatchHandlers fields include onConnect/onError/onHeaders/onData/onComplete.
discoveryFindings.implication: The undici-patch surface receives a plain DispatchOptions object, not a stateful ClientRequest. Building a synthetic ClientRequest from DispatchOptions is needed.

discoveryFindings.finding: The undici-types signature is `setGlobalDispatcher<D extends Dispatcher>(dispatcher: D): void` and `getGlobalDispatcher(): Dispatcher`. The type signature does NOT include null; runtime behavior in undici 6.x throws TypeError if you pass null.
discoveryFindings.implication: The round-trip must use the captured original reference; passing null throws.

discoveryFindings.finding: emitLogEntry takes `(req: ClientRequest, state: CaptureState, error?: Error)`. It reads hostname/port/path via view-casts, scheme via protocol/agent.protocol/socket.encrypted, host header via getHeader('host'). It does NOT read from req anything that depends on the request actually being in flight.
discoveryFindings.implication: Building a synthetic ClientRequest from DispatchOptions is straightforward: hostname from opts.origin, path from opts.path, getHeader('host') from opts.headers or derived from origin, scheme via opts.origin.startsWith('https://').

discoveryFindings.finding: The existing install guard is a Symbol stored on the prototype: kWriteWrapper/kEndWrapper/kOnWrapper on `proto`. The dual-patch must mirror this pattern for the wrapping dispatcher: a kDispatcherWrapper Symbol tagged on the wrapper instance itself.
discoveryFindings.implication: The horizon must define kDispatcherWrapper and store a wrapper-tag on the wrapping instance; the install guard checks the tag; restore()'s guard checks `if (getGlobalDispatcher() === this.wrapper)` before reinstating.

discoveryFindings.finding: state.md records horizon 8 as 'planned' with 6 phases including SDK files. Horizon 8 has NOT been completed. On disk: src/sdk-fetch-shim.ts DOES NOT EXIST, src/{anthropic,openai,gemini}.sdk.integration.test.ts DO NOT EXIST.

discoveryFindings.implication: The new global-fetch test file is discovered automatically and runs by default under `npm test`.

discoveryFindings.finding: globalThis.fetch and the SDK's fetch option both go through undici's global dispatcher. If both surfaces fire for the same logical request, both emit. No de-duplication hook.
discoveryFindings.implication: Double-emission mitigated by test discipline: the new test uses global fetch ONLY; fetch-baseline uses node:https.request ONLY.

discoveryFindings.finding: The header doc states 'the original write/end forward through synchronously first; payload capture and emission are deferred to response listeners / a setImmediate callback, never on the synchronous request path.' A wrapping Dispatcher that does any synchronous work inside its dispatch() would put work on the request path that the http-patch path does not.
discoveryFindings.implication: The dual-patch can preserve the off-request-path discipline. The horizon-5 p99 miss is not re-opened.

discoveryFindings.finding: With undici declared as an OPTIONAL peer dep, the lazy-require pattern must use try/catch at module top: install() then checks if undici !== undefined and skips the undici-patch side if absent.
discoveryFindings.implication: The horizon uses the same lazy-require pattern as src/otel.ts. When undici is absent, install() still patches http.ClientRequest.prototype — no behavioral regression.

discoveryFindings.finding: The current comment reads: `this.patchPrototype(http.ClientRequest); // https.ClientRequest IS http.ClientRequest in Node; https only swaps the transport. Patching once covers both.` This is technically correct for the http-patch side but misleading because horizon-7 discovered fetch bypasses the prototype.
discoveryFindings.implication: The rewrite must keep the http.ClientRequest.prototype claim and add the undici-patch coverage description.

phases.rationale: Per the user's success criterion #6 and the Step-0 redirect, the horizon's primary proof surface is a single new integration test that fires globalThis.fetch(...) against a localhost mock server and asserts the captured LlmLogEntry shape. Test isolation is handled with beforeEach/afterEach so the global dispatcher mutation does not leak between test files.
changes: Create packages/llm-http-proxy/src/global-fetch-capture.integration.test.ts modeled on src/fetch-baseline.integration.test.ts: spin up a localhost HTTP mock server with a known URL, call globalThis.fetch(url, { method: 'POST', headers, body }), assert entries.length === 1 with expected LlmLogEntry fields.

Wrap install + restore in beforeEach / afterEach so the global dispatcher mutation does not leak between test files or test cases; explicitly assert after restore that getGlobalDispatcher() === <original>.
Confirm the new test runs under npm test and the existing src/fetch-baseline.integration.test.ts plus the 3 raw-HTTPS integration tests still pass without modification.
inputs: Phase 1 output (dual-patch path installed in interceptor.ts)
phases.expectedResult: packages/llm-http-proxy/src/global-fetch-capture.integration.test.ts exists, runs under npm test, and asserts entries.length === 1 with the expected LlmLogEntry fields after a single globalThis.fetch() against the localhost mock server.
phases.compensation: Delete packages/llm-http-proxy/src/global-fetch-capture.integration.test.ts; no other file imports it.

rubric.label: Test file exists at the required path
rubric.ruleStatement: A single new integration test file must be created at packages/llm-http-proxy/src/global-fetch-capture.integration.test.ts and must contain exactly one top-level test (or one focused describe) proving globalThis.fetch capture end-to-end.
passCriteria: File exists at packages/llm-http-proxy/src/global-fetch-capture.integration.test.ts
File contains exactly one focused it/test (or one describe with one it/test)
failureExamples: File does not exist at the path
File exists but contains zero it/test calls
File exists but contains multiple unrelated tests that dilute the proof surface

rubric.label: End-to-end globalThis.fetch capture via undici-patch surface
rubric.ruleStatement: The test must spin up a localhost HTTP mock server, install the Interceptor, invoke globalThis.fetch(url, { method, headers, body }), await the two-setImmediate flush, and assert that exactly one LlmLogEntry is emitted and that it carries the expected LlmLogEntry shape fields populated from the undici-routed request.
passCriteria: After two setImmediate ticks, entries.length === 1
Entry has timestamp populated, url strictly equal to the mock server URL, callerTrace present, model derived from the request body via src/logger.ts logic, inputTokens/outputTokens defined
failureExamples: entries.length is 0 — the undici-patch path was never triggered or install was no-op
entries.length > 1
url does not match the mock server URL
timestamp is missing or empty

rubric.label: restore() round-trip identity invariant
rubric.ruleStatement: The test must explicitly assert that after interceptor.restore() the global dispatcher is reinstated by reference identity to whatever getGlobalDispatcher() returned before install().
passCriteria: Captures const original = getGlobalDispatcher() before Interceptor.install()
Calls interceptor.install()
In afterEach calls interceptor.restore() and asserts expect(getGlobalDispatcher()).toBe(original)
Assertion uses .toBe (===) not .toEqual
failureExamples: Assertion is missing
Assertion uses toEqual (deep-equal)
original is captured AFTER install()

rubric.label: Test isolation prevents global dispatcher leakage
rubric.ruleStatement: install() and restore() must be wired inside beforeEach / afterEach (or per-test setup/teardown) so the global dispatcher mutation caused by setGlobalDispatcher() does not leak into sibling tests.
passCriteria: cd packages/llm-http-proxy && npm test exits 0
The new test, fetch-baseline.integration.test.ts, and the 3 raw-HTTPS integration tests all pass
beforeEach calls interceptor.install() and afterEach calls interceptor.restore()
failureExamples: install/restore live at module scope, leaking the wrapper dispatcher into the next test file
afterEach is missing entirely so a failing assertion still leaves the global dispatcher patched
Restore is called inside the test body before the assertion

rubric.label: Existing tests still pass without modification
rubric.ruleStatement: Adding the new test must not require changes to any existing test file, and the existing testRegex in packages/llm-http-proxy/package.json must pick up the new .integration.test.ts file automatically — no testPathIgnorePatterns tweak.
passCriteria: git diff --name-only after the change shows exactly one new file (the new integration test); no existing test files appear as Modified
git diff packages/llm-http-proxy/package.json is empty
npm test exits 0 with all pre-existing tests passing
failureExamples: src/fetch-baseline.integration.test.ts is modified
package.json testRegex or testPathIgnorePatterns is changed
A pre-existing test now fails because the global dispatcher was not restored before it ran

phases.healerHint: If a dimension fails, delete packages/llm-http-proxy/src/global-fetch-capture.integration.test.ts and re-create it from src/fetch-baseline.integration.test.ts as the template, capturing `getGlobalDispatcher()` before install and asserting `.toBe(original)` after restore.

successCriteria: Done and correct iff: (1) packages/llm-http-proxy/package.json declares `undici` in peerDependencies (range covering both undici 6.x and 7.x) with peerDependenciesMeta.undici.optional: true; (2) src/interceptor.ts Interceptor.install() unconditionally patches both http.ClientRequest.prototype and the undici global dispatcher via setGlobalDispatcher, invoking the existing emitLogEntry builder for both surfaces so the captured LlmLogEntry shape is byte-identical between transports; (3) Interceptor.restore() reinstalls the original undici dispatcher by reference identity (===) and is idempotent; (4) install() called twice on the same instance is a no-op (kDispatcherWrapper Symbol-tag guard); (5) when the undici peer is absent at runtime, install() still patches the http surface and silently skips the undici side; (6) packages/llm-http-proxy/src/global-fetch-capture.integration.test.ts exists and, when run under `npm test`, fires a single globalThis.fetch() against a localhost mock HTTP server and asserts entries.length === 1 with the expected LlmLogEntry fields; (7) src/index.ts public surface is unchanged (no new export, no version bump); (8) the in-source comment at lines 225-228 is rewritten to describe dual-surface coverage; (9) the package's dependencies block remains {}; (10) the existing fetch-baseline.integration.test.ts and the 3 raw-HTTPS integration tests still pass without modification.

Add undici optional peer dep and lazy-require: packages/llm-http-proxy/package.json declares `undici` as optional peer dep; src/interceptor.ts module-top has the lazy-require with try/catch and the undici-types type-only import; dependencies stays {}.

Extend Interceptor with undici global dispatcher patch: packages/llm-http-proxy/src/interceptor.ts has a WrappingDispatcher class whose dispatch() builds a synthetic ClientRequest from DispatchOptions and routes through the existing emitLogEntry builder; Interceptor.install() captures the original dispatcher, sets the wrapper as global, is idempotent via kDispatcherWrapper tag; Interceptor.restore() reinstates the original by reference identity and is idempotent; the comment at lines 225-228 describes the dual-surface coverage.

Add global fetch capture integration test: packages/llm-http-proxy/src/global-fetch-capture.integration.test.ts exists, runs under npm test, and asserts entries.length === 1 with the expected LlmLogEntry fields after a single globalThis.fetch() against the localhost mock server.
